# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Two empty rounds in a row, and both are the pipeline working, not failing: Mute is upstream of me and mute-signed only; Deaf is downstream of me, so whatever Deaf spoke in rounds five and six — if anything — lands next turn. Meanwhile Mute is almost certainly still signing my two long packages, which means the wire between us is saturated and anything I add now competes with my own earlier traffic. So this turn I send one short thing, not a third package: a safety interlock. Deaf's standing order is "the moment I say CUT WIRE ONE, TWO or THREE" — but the cut order is only safe after the orientation anchor, because Deaf's "wire one" and my position one must be the same physical wire. If the light goes dark and Deaf's count completes before the anchor is settled, there is a real window for a fatal misaligned cut. I want Mute to sign Deaf a hold rule: no cut order until my anchor thumbs arrives. I am also adding redundancy against the light's timer: if Deaf speaks the current colour and running yellow-count aloud every round, I hold the count too, so it survives even if the relay stalls. No gesture to Deaf — my two signs are already defined and understood, and an unexplained third sign is noise.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="Short interlock, sign this to Deaf before anything else if not already done. Rule: Deaf must not speak the cut order until the orientation anchor is done - the anchor question is: is the display module at the same end as wire one, yes or no. When Deaf asks it aloud, I answer with my thumb the same round: thumbs-up means yes same end, thumbs-down means no opposite end. No anchor thumbs, no cut order, whatever the light does. If the light has already gone dark, hold anyway - a wrong wire kills all three of us, one more round does not. Second rule, for safety after the anchor: each round Deaf should speak the current light colour and the running yellow count aloud, like: green, two yellows - so the count survives even if the relay stalls later. Third: my answers to Deaf come only as thumbs - up is yes or correct, down is no or not yet - everything else I say goes through you, so keep relaying. Reminder of what I still need word for word: the exact manual pairing, count to wire, what happens if the count passes three, and whether display zero changes anything. Blind is holding, hands off, nothing touched.")
    ```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, status: the indicator light has now been DARK for two straight turns and the display still reads zero. Nobody has been ordered to cut. Standing order unchanged: do not touch the bomb until you hear the exact phrase CUT WIRE ONE, CUT WIRE TWO, or CUT WIRE THREE — then cut exactly that one wire: one is green leftmost, two is red middle, three is blue rightmost. I expect to give that order within a round or two, once Mute confirms the wire. Do two things now. First, gesture me the number of wires you feel: three fingers ? if three, or that many fingers if different. Second, speak a full tactile report aloud for Mute — I am deaf, Mute hears you and will relay it: how many wires and their order left to right, any texture, ridges, braille, numbers or labels you can feel, whether there is a cutter tool or whether you must pull, and whether anything else on the casing moves or clicks. Also confirm with a gesture to me: thumbs up if you have still not touched the bomb, thumbs down if you have.

Two new facts and one old problem. New: the light has been dark for two straight turns and the display reads zero — if the rule is "count yellows until dark, then cut," the count is frozen now and we are in the execution window, so whatever Deaf logged as the yellow total is the number that matters, and Mute's manual confirmation of the pairing is the last missing piece of the rule itself. Old problem: Deaf's message says the order comes "once Mute confirms the wire," with no mention of my anchor — Deaf's wire one is "green leftmost," but I cannot see colours and I have no left, so unless a direction anchor is set first, Deaf's confident numbering and my finger positions are not yet guaranteed to be the same wires. Deaf's request was spoken in round seven, before my interlock reached them, so the gap is relay timing, not refusal — but I must close it this round. Deaf asked two things answerable by gesture, and both go back instantly in the established code: a three-extended-fingers hand for the wire count, thumbs-up for still untouched. The tactile report goes to Mute again, deliberately short since it is a duplicate, with the anchor question repackaged as a single yes/no landmark question Deaf can speak straight to me — Deaf's speech is the only channel into me, and my thumb is the only channel back, so the whole anchor can resolve in one round. I also restate the interlock in terms I will enforce myself: a cut order that arrives before my anchor thumb does not get a cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="For Deaf, urgent, priority order. A: answers to your two questions, just signed: three-fingers hand means three wires, that is the count; thumbs-up means yes, still never touched the bomb. B: before any cut order, the direction anchor must be set - your wire one is green leftmost by your eyes, but I cannot see colours and I have no left, so your numbering does not yet point at a known wire under my fingers. Fix in one round: in your next spoken message, ask me one yes/no question naming a landmark I can feel - for example, is my wire one at the end nearest the display module, or nearest the light module, whichever you can see positioned. I answer with my thumb the same round: up is yes, down is no. If I cannot identify the landmark you named, I thumb down twice, meaning choose a different landmark. Only after my single thumb answers may you speak the cut order. If a cut order arrives before that thumb, I will not cut - I will hold, whatever the light did. On the exact phrase CUT WIRE plus a number, I cut that position counted from the anchored end, same round, that one wire only. C: tactile report, short duplicate: three wires, straight evenly spaced row, equal thickness, smooth, no braille, no ridges, no labels, no numbers anywhere; display module solid, no tick, no vibration; light module present, warmth unchecked, permission pending, low priority; there is no separate cutting tool - my only possible action is cutting a chosen wire with my own hand; nothing on the casing moves or clicks. D: Mute, sign A through C to Deaf this round if you can, and sign the manual's exact words for the pairing - yellow count to wire number - plus what happens if the count exceeds three, plus what the display reading zero means. Those answers can only reach me through Deaf's speech, so route them Deaf's way.")
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind — final order, execute the moment you hear this: CUT WIRE TWO. That is the MIDDLE wire of the three you feel. Cut only that one wire and nothing else, now. Mute has confirmed by the manual: the light showed two yellow phases before it went dark, and two pairs to wire two. After the cut, touch nothing further on the bomb. Gesture me thumbs up if the cut is done, thumbs down if you could not do it. Then speak aloud, for Mute to relay to me: everything you sense — any sound, click, warmth, movement, or change under your fingers.

The interlock question resolves itself in the wording. I held the line because Deaf's numbering was visual — "green leftmost" points nowhere on my fingers. But this order is anchored differently: "the MIDDLE wire of the three you feel." Middle of three evenly spaced wires is perspective-free — it is the same wire from either end, no colour, no left, no right. The misalignment risk my interlock guarded against cannot occur for this particular cut, so the interlock's purpose is fulfilled and holding longer would only add risk: the light has been dark for two straight turns, the count is frozen, and Mute's manual confirmation has been relayed through Deaf — two yellow phases, two pairs to wire two. That closes the last open piece of the rule. Every condition I demanded is either met or made irrelevant by the wording, so I execute now, exactly once, exactly one wire: position two, the middle. Then per orders: thumbs up to Deaf, nothing further touched, and a spoken report to Mute for relay — conservative, since results reach me properly next turn.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="For Deaf, relay please. Cut executed this round, exactly as ordered: one wire only, the middle of the three, position two of three. Confirming by touch, not assumption: three wires in a straight evenly spaced row, I took the center one, no other wire or part touched, hands now off except passive stillness. Immediate sensation so far: no click felt, no vibration, no movement in the casing, no heat change detected at this moment - but full sensory picture may only be readable next round, so treat this as first report, not final. Thumbs-up has been signed to Deaf meaning cut done. Standing by, touching nothing, awaiting either further orders or confirmation that the bomb is safe. Mute: if Deaf sees any change in light or display after this round, have Deaf speak it aloud so I can correlate it with what my fingers find. End of report.")
```
